extracted.intended_audience: general public; marketing students and professionals interested in brand case studies
extracted.subtask_description: A company web article recounting the New Coke launch and aftermath, explaining the business context, decisions, consumer reactions, and lessons for brand and marketing strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-energize the brand and the category
rubrics_metrics.description: The company intended to 're-energize its Coca‑Cola brand and the cola category in its largest market, the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position product changes as part of a broader effort to revive brand relevance and category momentum. Recognize that ambition to re-energize can justify major changes, but balance with potential consumer backlash and legacy value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use large-scale taste testing to guide formula changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The fabled secret formula for Coca‑Cola was changed, adopting a formula preferred in taste tests of nearly 200,000 consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect extensive consumer preference data (e.g., large taste tests) to inform product changes. However, be aware these tests measure preference in controlled settings and may not capture deeper emotional attachments or real-world consumption contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for consumers' emotional bond and brand heritage
rubrics_metrics.description: What these tests didn't show... was the bond consumers felt with their Coca‑Cola — something they didn't want anyone, including The Coca‑Cola Company, tampering with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate not just functional preference but sentimental and identity-based ties to a product. Failure to respect heritage can trigger strong reactions (protests, hoarding, campaigns) that quantitative tests may miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take intelligent risks
rubrics_metrics.description: "Taking intelligent risks" — the decision was later characterized as a prime example of taking intelligent risks and urged employees to take such risks to build value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage calculated risk-taking to drive growth and signal commitment to value creation. Accept that some intelligent risks may fail, but can still yield strategic learning and long-term benefits if managed properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and provide channels for consumer feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls flooded in... By June 1985, The Coca‑Cola Company was getting 1,500 calls a day on its consumer hotline, compared with 400 a day before the taste change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain robust, responsive consumer-feedback mechanisms (hotlines, customer service, social monitoring). Track volumes and sentiment as early warning signals; treat feedback as actionable intelligence for product and communication responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to reverse course quickly when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The return of original formula Coca‑Cola on July 11, 1985, put the cap on 79 days that revolutionized the soft-drink industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design decision processes with agility and contingency plans so reversals or corrective actions can be executed promptly. A timely reversal can restore consumer trust and limit long-term damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate positioning and campaigns for coexisting variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Coca‑Cola classic was sold alongside Coca‑Cola ('new Coke'), and the two brands had distinct advertising campaigns, with the youthful, leading-edge 'Catch the Wave' campaign for the new taste of Coke and the emotional 'Red, White and You' for Coca‑Cola classic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offering multiple product variants, use separate brand positioning and tailored campaigns to avoid consumer confusion and to target distinct audience segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand market context and long-term competitive trends
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1985... The Coca‑Cola Company's share lead over its chief competitor... had been slowly slipping for 15 consecutive years. The cola category in general was lethargic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground major product and marketing decisions in a clear analysis of market share trends, category health, and competitive dynamics. Remedies should address underlying structural issues, not just surface symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and manage media amplification of major announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: The announcement of the return of 'old' Coca‑Cola... led two network newscasts and made the front page of virtually every major newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect major product moves to attract intense media attention. Prepare communications strategies that anticipate amplification—both positive and negative—and plan messaging to steer public narrative.
